regime: Aligned down. Both NQ and ES now read short below falling stops after the week's split resolved lower. Volatility is still expanding. Gold rests above its rising stop and crude leads higher. Normal-to-reduced risk.
summary: The split finally broke, and it broke down. NQ closed 29,317, its second straight day under a falling stop, and this time the S&P came with it. ES lost its 7,706 stop and closed 7,668, so both indices now read short and the week's NQ-versus-ES divergence is gone. Gold took a breather after its big run, closing 4,540.9 just under flat but still above a rising stop, so that uptrend is only resting. Crude was the bright spot, up 2.1% to 86.21, clearing its prior high and holding well above its stop. Volatility kept expanding, with the Nasdaq hourly ATR near 105 versus 92 on Wednesday and the mid-60s on Monday.
psychology: When a divergence resolves, do not fight the resolution. For two days NQ was short while ES stayed long, and plenty of traders kept buying the S&P because it looked stronger. Today it flipped and joined the weak one. A split is a warning, not a trade. When it closes the gap you follow the side that wins, you do not marry the side you liked.
